questions.question: That's the end of the situation. Have you ever had a problem when you booked tickets or made a reservation? Tell me what happened, how you dealt with it, and how it turned out.

il.text: Yes, I had a problem last year. I bought concert tickets online. But I chose the wrong day. I called the company. They changed my tickets. I was very happy. It was okay.
One time I booked a restaurant for my mom's birthday. But when we went there, there was no reservation. We waited thirty minutes. Then we got a table. The food was good.

im1.text: I remember one problem last summer. I booked train tickets to Busan for my family vacation. But when we got to the station, I saw the tickets were for the next day. I was so embarrassed. I talked to the staff at the counter, and they were very kind. They changed the tickets to a later train that day. We waited one hour, but we arrived safely. Now I always check the date twice.

A few months ago, I had a problem with a hotel reservation. I booked a room online for a weekend trip with my friends. When we arrived, the hotel said they didn't have our reservation. I showed them the email on my phone. After about twenty minutes, they found the problem and gave us a room. It was a little stressful, but in the end, everything was fine.

im2.text: Yes, I had a similar problem about two years ago. I wanted to see a famous musical with my sister, so I bought two tickets online. On the day of the show, we got dressed up and went to the theater. But when we showed our tickets, the staff told us they were for the afternoon show, not the evening show. We had already missed it! I was so upset. I explained the situation, and the manager was really kind. She found two seats for the evening show, but we had to pay a small fee. After that, I learned to read my tickets carefully.

I had a problem like that when I booked a camping site last fall. I reserved a spot for my family on a website, and I paid in advance. But when we arrived at the campsite, another family was already in our spot. The staff checked the system and said the website made a mistake. At first, I was really angry because it was getting dark. But the staff apologized and gave us a better spot near the lake. They also gave us a discount. In the end, we had a great time, but I still remember how stressed I was.

im3.text: Actually, something like that happened to me last winter. I was planning a ski trip with my college friends, so I booked a cabin near a ski resort about a month in advance. On the day we arrived, we were really excited, but the owner told us the cabin was double-booked. Another group had already checked in. I was shocked, and honestly, I was pretty angry because it was snowing and we had nowhere to go. I asked him to find us another place nearby, and luckily, he called his friend who had a small guesthouse. It wasn't as nice as the cabin, but it was warm, and he gave us half of our money back. Looking back, it's a funny story now.
phrases: something like that happened to me

im3.text: Yes, I remember a problem I had with concert tickets about three years ago. My favorite band was coming to Korea, and the tickets sold out in five minutes. I was lucky to get two tickets, and I was so happy. But a week later, I got an email saying my payment didn't go through. I was really worried, so I called the ticket office right away. The staff said they could keep my seats for one hour if I paid again. I quickly paid with a different card, and it worked. On the day of the concert, I enjoyed every minute. Since then, I always check my payment right after I buy tickets.

ih.text: Yes, I've had a few problems like that, but the one I remember most happened during a trip to Jeju Island two years ago. My friends and I had booked a rental car online, and we were supposed to pick it up at the airport. When we got to the rental counter, though, the staff couldn't find our reservation anywhere. Apparently, I'd made the booking for the following month by mistake. It was peak season, so they didn't have a single car left. At first, I panicked, because our whole plan depended on that car. But I stayed calm and asked the staff if they could recommend another company. They made a couple of phone calls for us and found a small local company with one car available. It was more expensive and kind of old, but it got us around the island just fine. Since then, I always double-check every date before I click the payment button.

That reminds me of something that happened when I tried to book a table for my parents' thirtieth wedding anniversary. I chose a nice Italian restaurant downtown and made a reservation by phone about two weeks in advance. On the night of the dinner, we all dressed up and arrived right on time, but the host said there was no reservation under my name. I was so embarrassed, especially because my whole family was standing behind me. I showed him the confirmation text I had received, and he realized that a new employee had written the wrong date. The manager came out and apologized several times. They set up a table for us by the window in about fifteen minutes, and they even gave us free dessert. In the end, my parents said it was one of the best dinners they'd ever had, so it all worked out.

al.text: Oh, definitely. The most memorable one was a couple of years ago, when I was planning a trip to Busan with my college roommates to watch the fireworks festival. Since the festival is incredibly popular, I booked a hotel room near the beach almost three months in advance and even paid the full amount up front. When we finally arrived that evening, exhausted after a five-hour drive, the front desk clerk told us they'd overbooked and didn't have a room for us. I was honestly furious at first, because there was no way we'd find another room nearby on festival night. Still, I tried to stay polite and asked what they could do to make it right. After talking with the manager for a while, they arranged a room at their sister hotel about ten minutes away, paid for our taxi, and refunded half of what we'd paid. It wasn't the ocean view we'd hoped for, but we still watched the fireworks from the beach. Looking back, it taught me that staying calm usually gets you a better result than losing your temper.

I actually went through something pretty similar last spring. I'd bought tickets for a big baseball game, the opening game of the season, for my dad and me. He's a huge fan, so I wanted it to be a special day for him. A few days before the game, though, I got a message saying the game had been moved to a different stadium because of construction, and that our seats might not be available. I was really worried, so I called the ticket office right away. The first person I talked to wasn't very helpful, and I was getting pretty frustrated. However, I called back later, explained the situation more clearly, and asked to speak to a supervisor. She was much more understanding and patient. She moved us to seats that were even closer to the field and didn't charge us anything extra. On the day of the game, my dad couldn't stop smiling the whole time. That experience taught me that being persistent, but still polite, can really pay off.
phrases: I actually went through something pretty similar
asked to speak to a supervisor

questions.tip_ko: 언제, 무슨 일, 어떻게 해결, 결과 순서로 과거 시제를 지켜 말해요. 마지막에 배운 점 한 문장을 붙이면 마무리가 깔끔해요.

phone.situation_ko: 새 휴대폰을 사려고 매장에 전화해 묻고, 산 휴대폰이 켜지지 않는 문제를 해결해요.

questions.question: I'd like to give you a situation and ask you to act it out. You want to buy a new phone. Call the electronics store and ask three or four questions to get the information you need before you buy one.

il.text: Hello. I want a new phone. Do you have new phones? How much are they? Can I pay by card? What time do you close? Thank you.
Hi. I need a new phone. Is it expensive? Do you have a black one? Can I buy it today? Thank you very much.

im1.text: Hello, I'm calling because I want to buy a new phone. First, what phones do you have now? And how much is the newest one? Also, do you have any discounts this month? Lastly, what time does the store close today? I want to visit after work. Thank you.

Hi, I'm thinking about buying a new phone. Can I ask you a few questions? Do you sell phones with a big screen? How long does the battery last? Can I pay in monthly payments? And can I try the phone in the store? Thanks a lot.
phrases: Can I ask you a few questions

im2.text: Hi, I'm calling about buying a new phone. My old phone is really slow. Could you tell me which models you have right now? I'm especially interested in a phone with a good camera. How much is the cheapest one? Do you have any special deals? And one more thing, can you move my data from my old phone? Thank you so much.

Hello, I'd like to ask a few questions about phones. I'm planning to buy a new one this week. First, which phone is the most popular these days? Second, is there a difference in price if I buy it online or in the store? Third, does the phone come with a case and a charger? Finally, how long is the warranty? I want to make a good choice, so thank you for your help.
phrases: I'd like to ask a few questions
I want to make a good choice

im3.text: Hi there, I'm calling because I'm thinking about getting a new phone, and I have a few questions before I come in. My current phone is about four years old, and the battery dies really fast. First, could you recommend a model with a long battery life? Second, what's the price range for that kind of phone? I'd like to keep it under about eight hundred dollars. Third, do you offer any trade-in program for old phones? And lastly, are you open on Sunday? Thanks.
phrases: I have a few questions before I come in
I'd like to keep it under

im3.text: Hello, I saw your store's ad, and I'm interested in buying a new phone. Could I ask you a couple of things? To begin with, I'd like to know what models are on sale right now. I heard there's a holiday discount, so how much can I save? Also, I'm not very good with technology, so would someone at the store help me set up the phone? And finally, if I don't like it, can I return it within a week? Thank you so much for your time.
phrases: Thank you so much for your time

ih.text: Hi. I'm calling because I'm planning to buy a new phone soon, and I'd like to get some information before I visit your store. First of all, could you tell me which models you'd recommend for someone who takes a lot of photos? Second, I'm on a bit of a budget, so I'm wondering what the price difference is between the latest model and last year's model. Also, do you have a trade-in program? I'd love to get some money back for my old phone. And lastly, if I buy one, how long would it take to transfer my contacts and photos? Thanks a lot for your help.
phrases: I'd like to get some information before
I'm on a bit of a budget
I'm wondering what the price difference is
I'd love to get some money back

ih.text: Hello, is this the electronics store on Main Street? Great. I'm thinking about buying a new phone, and I was hoping you could help me with a few questions. To start with, do you have the newest models in stock right now, or would I need to order one? I've heard they sell out quickly. Next, I'd like to know whether there are any discounts if I pay the full price at once instead of monthly. I'm also curious about the warranty. If the screen breaks, is that covered? Finally, could I come in this evening to try a few phones before deciding? Thank you, that's really helpful.
phrases: I was hoping you could help me with

al.text: Hi, good morning. I'm calling because I'm in the market for a new phone, and I'd like to narrow down my options before I come in. First, could you tell me which models you'd recommend for someone who uses their phone for work emails, video calls, and a lot of photos? Second, I'm trying to stick to a reasonable budget, so I'd like to know if last year's models are being sold at a discount now that the new ones are out. I'm also wondering whether you offer a trade-in program, and if so, roughly how much I could get for an older phone. Lastly, if I buy something today, is there someone who can help me transfer all my data? I really appreciate your help.
phrases: I'd like to narrow down my options
I'm trying to stick to a reasonable budget

al.text: Hello there. I'm planning to replace my phone soon, and since I'd rather not spend an hour wandering around the store, I thought I'd call ahead with a few questions. To begin with, could you tell me which phones you currently have in stock? Assuming you have them, I'd also like to know how the prices compare between buying the phone outright and paying in monthly installments, because I want to see which option ends up cheaper in the long run. Another thing I'm curious about is the return policy. If I use the phone for a few days and realize it's not right for me, can I exchange it? And finally, what are your hours this weekend? I'd like to drop by on Saturday morning. Thanks.
phrases: Another thing I'm curious about is

questions.tip_ko: 인사 → 전화한 이유 → 질문 3~4개 → 감사 인사 순서로 해요. First, Also, Lastly로 질문을 나누면 듣기 편해요.

questions.question: I'm sorry, but there is a problem I need you to resolve. You bought the phone, but when you got home, you found that the screen does not turn on. Call the store, explain the situation, and suggest two or three ways to solve the problem.

il.text: Hello. I bought a phone today. But the screen does not work. It does not turn on. Can I change it? Or can you fix it? Or can I get my money back? Please help me.
phrases: But the screen does not work

il.text: Hi. I have a problem. I bought a new phone at your store. The phone is broken. The screen is black. I want a new one. Or please give me my money. Thank you.

im1.text: Hello, I bought a phone at your store this afternoon. When I got home, I tried to turn it on, but the screen stayed black. I charged it for one hour, but it still doesn't work. So I have some ideas. First, can I come back and change it for a new one? Or, if you don't have the same phone, can I get a refund? Please let me know. Thank you.

Hi, I'm calling about a problem with my new phone. I bought it today, but the screen doesn't turn on at all. I tried everything, but nothing happened. I'm very disappointed. Can you send someone to check it? If not, I can visit the store tomorrow and get a new phone. Or you can give me a different model. What do you think?
phrases: I'm calling about a problem with

im2.text: Hello, this is the customer who bought a phone at your store about two hours ago. I'm sorry to bother you, but I have a problem. When I got home and pressed the power button, the screen didn't turn on. I charged it and tried again, but it's still completely black. I think the phone might be broken. I have a few suggestions. First, I can bring it back tomorrow morning and exchange it for a new one. Second, if you don't have the same model in stock, I'd like a full refund. Or maybe you could check it at the service center today. Please let me know what's possible.
phrases: I'm sorry to bother you, but
I think the phone might be broken
Please let me know what's possible

im2.text: Hi, I bought a new phone from your store this afternoon, and unfortunately there's a problem with it. The screen won't turn on, even after I charged it fully. I also tried restarting it, but nothing happened. Since it's a brand-new phone, I don't think I should have to pay for repairs. So I'd like to ask for one of these options. Could I exchange it for a new phone? If that's not possible, could you give me a refund? Another option is to lend me a phone while you fix mine. Thank you for understanding.
phrases: and unfortunately there's a problem with it
I don't think I should have to

im3.text: Hi, I'm calling because there's a problem with the phone I bought from your store earlier today. I was really excited to set it up, but when I pressed the power button, nothing happened. The screen stayed completely black. I plugged it in for about an hour and tried again, and I even held down the buttons to restart it, but it still won't turn on. I think it's a defect, so I'd like to solve this as quickly as possible. I have a couple of ideas. First, I could come back to the store tomorrow and exchange it for a new one. If you don't have one in stock, I'd prefer a full refund. Or, if you think it can be fixed easily, maybe a technician could look at it today. Which option works best for you?
phrases: I have a couple of ideas
Which option works best for you

im3.text: Hello, I bought a phone from you this afternoon, and I'm afraid it isn't working. When I got home, I took it out of the box and tried to turn it on, but the screen didn't light up at all. I tried charging it with a different cable too, just in case, but there was no change. I need my phone for work tomorrow, so this is pretty urgent for me. Could we try a few things? Maybe you could walk me through some steps over the phone to see if it's a simple setting. If that doesn't work, I'd like to exchange it tonight before you close. And if there's no stock left, a refund would be fine. Thanks for your help.
phrases: and I'm afraid it isn't working
this is pretty urgent for me

ih.text: Hi, good evening. My name is on the receipt, but basically I bought a new phone from your store this afternoon, and I'm calling because there's a serious problem with it. When I got home and opened the box, everything looked fine, but when I pressed the power button, the screen didn't turn on. I assumed the battery was empty, so I charged it for over an hour. After that, I tried restarting it by holding both buttons, like the manual says, but the screen is still completely black. I can hear a small sound when I plug it in, so I think the phone is on, but the screen itself might be broken. Since it's brand new, I'd really like to get this fixed quickly. Would it be possible to exchange it for a new one tomorrow morning? If not, I could also accept a full refund. Or, if you have a repair center nearby, maybe they could check it today while I wait. Please let me know which option is best.
phrases: I assumed the battery was empty
the screen itself might be broken

ih.text: Hello, I'm calling about the phone I bought at your store around three o'clock today. I hate to say this, but it seems to be defective. I set it up as soon as I got home, and everything was fine for about ten minutes. Then the screen suddenly went black, and now it won't turn back on no matter what I do. I've tried charging it, using a different outlet, and restarting it, but nothing works. To be honest, I'm a little frustrated, because I paid quite a lot for this phone and I was really looking forward to using it. I can think of a few ways we could solve this. The simplest would be for me to bring it back and swap it for a new one. If that model is sold out, I'd like either a full refund or a similar model at the same price. Or, if you'd prefer, you could send it to the service center, as long as you lend me a phone in the meantime.
phrases: I hate to say this, but
To be honest, I'm a little frustrated
I can think of a few ways

al.text: Hi, good evening. I'm sorry to call so close to closing time, but I bought a phone from your store this afternoon, and unfortunately it seems to be defective. Let me explain what happened. As soon as I got home, I unboxed it and pressed the power button, but the screen didn't respond at all. At first I assumed the battery was simply empty, so I left it on the charger for over an hour. When that didn't help, I tried a forced restart, following the instructions in the manual, and I even switched to a different cable and outlet in case the charger was the problem. The phone vibrates slightly when I plug it in, so it seems to have power, but the display stays completely black. I suspect it's a hardware issue with the screen. Since the phone is less than a day old, I'd rather not wait weeks for a repair. Ideally, I'd like to exchange it for a new one tomorrow morning. If the same model isn't available, I'd be happy with a comparable phone or a full refund. Which of those would work for you?
phrases: I'm sorry to call so close to closing time
I suspect it's a hardware issue

al.text: Hello, I'm hoping you can help me with a problem. I picked up a new phone at your store earlier today, and I'm afraid it isn't working properly. The moment I got home, I tried to turn it on, and the screen stayed completely dark. Thinking the battery might be drained, I charged it for a good hour and then tried again, but there was still nothing. I also searched online and tried a couple of troubleshooting tips, like holding down the volume and power buttons together, but none of them made any difference. I have to say I'm pretty disappointed, because I chose your store specifically for its good reviews. That said, I'm sure we can sort this out. I see three possible solutions. The first, and easiest for me, would be a straight exchange for a new unit. The second would be a full refund, in case you're out of stock. And the third would be a repair, but only if you could provide a loaner phone, since I rely on mine for work. Could you let me know which option you can offer?
phrases: I'm hoping you can help me with a problem
Thinking the battery might be drained
That said, I'm sure we can sort this out

questions.tip_ko: 문제 상황을 언제, 무엇이, 어떻게 안 되는지 구체적으로 설명하고, 대안을 First, Or, If not으로 두세 개 내요.

questions.question: That's the end of the situation. Have you ever had a problem with something you bought, like an electronic device? Tell me what happened and how you solved the problem.

il.text: Yes, I had a problem. Last year, I bought headphones. They did not work. One side had no sound. I went back to the store. They gave me new headphones. I was happy.
Two years ago, I bought a laptop online. It was very slow. I called the company. They said send it back. I sent it. They fixed it. It took two weeks.

im1.text: Yes, I had a similar problem last year. I bought wireless earbuds online. When they arrived, the left earbud didn't work. I was really upset because I wanted to use them on my trip. I called the customer center and explained the problem. They told me to send them back. About one week later, I got new earbuds. They worked well. After that, I always check things right away.

I remember a problem with my first laptop. A few months after I bought it, the keyboard stopped working. Some keys didn't type at all. I took it to the service center near my house. The staff checked it and said it was a small problem. They fixed it in one day, and it was free because of the warranty. I was very relieved.

im2.text: Yes, actually, something similar happened to me about two years ago. I bought a new tablet for my online classes. On the first day, it worked fine, but on the second day, it suddenly stopped charging. I tried a different charger, but it still didn't work. I was really stressed because I had an important class that week. So I went back to the store with the receipt and explained everything. At first, the staff wanted to send it for repair, but I said I needed it right away. Luckily, they agreed to give me a new one. Since then, I always keep my receipts.

I had a bad experience with a washing machine a few years ago. My family bought a new one, but after a week, it started making a really loud noise. It also stopped in the middle of washing. We called the company, and they sent a technician to our house. He said one part was broken, but he didn't have the part with him. So we had to wait another week. During that time, I washed my clothes at a laundromat. It was annoying, but in the end, the machine was fixed for free.
phrases: I had a bad experience with
It was annoying, but in the end

im3.text: Yes, I actually had a pretty frustrating experience with a laptop last year. I ordered it online because the price was much cheaper than in stores. When it arrived, it looked perfect, but after a few days, the screen started flickering whenever I opened a video. At first, I thought it was a software problem, so I updated everything, but it kept happening. I contacted the online shop, and they told me to send it to the manufacturer's service center. That took almost three weeks, and I had to borrow my brother's old computer for my assignments. When I finally got it back, they had replaced the whole screen, and it's been fine since. The experience taught me that cheaper isn't always better, and now I prefer buying expensive things in person.
phrases: I actually had a pretty frustrating experience
When I finally got it back

im3.text: I remember one time when I bought a smartwatch as a birthday gift for my dad. I was really excited to give it to him, but when he opened the box, the watch wouldn't connect to his phone. We spent almost an hour trying different settings, and my dad started to feel bad because he thought he was doing something wrong. The next day, I took it back to the store and showed the staff the problem. They tested it with another phone and found that the watch was defective. They apologized and gave me a new one right away, plus a small discount coupon. My dad has been using it every day since then. I was glad the store handled it so quickly.
phrases: I was glad the store handled it

ih.text: Yes, I've had a few problems like that, but the one I remember most happened about a year ago with a robot vacuum cleaner. I'd saved up for a while to buy it, and for the first two weeks, it was amazing. Then one day, it started spinning in circles in the middle of the living room and wouldn't return to its charging station. I tried resetting it and cleaning the sensors, but nothing changed. When I called the customer service center, I had to wait on hold for almost forty minutes, which was really frustrating. The agent finally told me to send it in for repair, but it would take two weeks. I explained that it was still brand new and asked for an exchange instead. At first she said that wasn't possible, but after I mentioned that I'd bought it less than a month ago, she checked their policy and agreed. A new one arrived a few days later. Since then, I always read the return policy carefully before buying anything expensive.
phrases: the one I remember most happened
I'd saved up for a while
At first she said that wasn't possible, but

ih.text: Actually, something very similar happened to me last spring. I bought a new pair of noise-canceling headphones before a long business trip. The night before my flight, I opened the box and found that the noise-canceling function didn't work at all. It just made a strange buzzing sound. I didn't have time to go back to the store, so I had to use my old earphones on the plane, which was disappointing. When I got back a week later, I went straight to the store with the headphones and the receipt. The manager tested them and agreed that they were defective, but they didn't have the same model in stock anymore. He offered me two choices: wait for a new shipment or choose a slightly better model for the same price. Of course, I took the better model. In the end, it worked out well, but I learned to test new electronics right away instead of waiting until the last minute.
phrases: something very similar happened to me
In the end, it worked out well, but

al.text: I've had a few issues with electronics over the years, but the one that really sticks with me involved a laptop I bought right before my final exams in university. I'd been using an old, painfully slow computer for years, so I finally treated myself to a decent model. For about a week, everything was perfect. Then, two days before a major deadline, the laptop started shutting down without warning, sometimes in the middle of typing. Naturally, I panicked, because my entire thesis was on it. Fortunately, I'd been backing up my files, so I didn't lose anything, but I still needed a working computer immediately. I took it to the store where I'd bought it, and the staff initially wanted to send it off for a repair that would take ten days. I calmly explained my situation, showed them a video I'd recorded of the problem, and pointed out that it was well within the exchange period. After a short discussion with the manager, they agreed to replace it on the spot. Looking back, I think staying calm and having clear evidence made all the difference.
phrases: the one that really sticks with me

al.text: Yes, and it was a bit of a saga, to be honest. A couple of years ago, I ordered a new phone online during a big sale. The price was great, but when the package arrived, the phone inside had a tiny crack in the corner of the screen. At first, I wasn't sure whether it had happened during delivery or before it was shipped, and that turned out to be the main problem. The online store said it was the delivery company's responsibility, and the delivery company said it was the store's. I spent almost a week going back and forth between them, which was incredibly frustrating. Eventually, I realized I needed to be more organized. I took clear photos of the box and the crack, wrote down the dates and names of everyone I'd talked to, and sent one detailed email to the store's customer service team. Within two days, they apologized and sent me a replacement, along with a gift card for the trouble. That experience taught me that being persistent and keeping records is the best way to deal with these kinds of problems.
phrases: it was a bit of a saga
that turned out to be the main problem

questions.tip_ko: 롤플레이 마지막 문항은 비슷한 경험을 묻는 질문이에요. 무슨 물건이었는지, 어떤 문제였는지, 어떻게 해결했는지를 과거형으로 말해요.

questions.question: You indicated in the survey that you enjoy going to cafés. Describe a café you like to visit. Where is it, what does it look like inside, and what makes it special to you?

il.text: I like a small café near my office. It is on the second floor. Inside, there are wooden tables and many plants. The music is quiet. The coffee is good and not expensive. I go there often.
My favorite café is in my neighborhood. It is very bright. It has big windows. There are comfortable sofas. They sell cake and cookies. The staff are kind. I love this café.

im1.text: I want to talk about a small café near my office. It is on the second floor of an old building, so it is quiet. When you go inside, you can see wooden tables, warm lights, and a lot of green plants. There is a big window, and you can see the street. The music is soft, so I can read or study there. The coffee is good, and the price is not bad. I go there about three times a week.

My favorite café is in my neighborhood, about five minutes from my house. It is not very big, but it is very bright because it has large windows. Inside, there are comfortable sofas and some long tables for people who work on laptops. The owner bakes cakes and cookies every morning, so the café always smells sweet. The staff are very friendly. I feel comfortable there, like it is my second home.
phrases: about five minutes from my house
like it is my second home

im2.text: I'd like to tell you about a small café near my office. It's on the second floor of an old brick building, so most people don't even know it's there. When you walk in, you see wooden tables, warm yellow lights, and lots of green plants hanging from the ceiling. There's a big window seat where you can look down at the street. The music is always soft jazz, so it's a great place to read or think. The coffee is really good, and the owner remembers my order. That's why I keep going back.
phrases: I'd like to tell you about
That's why I keep going back

im2.text: The café I visit most is in my neighborhood, just five minutes from my apartment. It's not very big, but it feels open and bright because the front wall is all glass. Inside, there are a few comfortable sofas and a long wooden table where people work on their laptops. The owner bakes everything herself, so every morning the café smells like fresh bread and cookies. What makes it special is the atmosphere. It's quiet and relaxing, and the staff are always friendly. For me, it's like a second living room.
phrases: The café I visit most is

im3.text: The café I'd like to describe is a small place near my office. It's hidden on the second floor of an old brick building, so if you don't know about it, you'll walk right past it. As soon as you go up the stairs, you smell fresh coffee. Inside, there are mismatched wooden tables, warm yellow lights, and so many plants that it almost feels like a greenhouse. My favorite spot is the window seat, because I can watch people walking down the street. The owner always plays soft jazz, and she remembers what everyone usually orders. It's the kind of place that makes you slow down for a while.
phrases: so if you don't know about it
It's the kind of place that

im3.text: I'd like to talk about the café in my neighborhood, because I practically live there on weekends. It's only five minutes from my apartment. The café isn't big, but the whole front is made of glass, so it's always full of natural light. There are a few deep sofas by the window and a long shared table in the back where people study or work on laptops. The owner bakes all the desserts herself, so the place smells like butter and cinnamon every morning. More than the coffee, though, I love the atmosphere. It's calm, cozy, and nobody rushes you to leave. I usually stay there for a few hours with a book and a cup of coffee.
phrases: the whole front is made of glass

ih.text: The café I want to describe is a tiny place near my office that I discovered almost by accident. It's on the second floor of an old brick building, and the only sign is a small chalkboard by the entrance, so most people walk right past it. As soon as you climb the narrow stairs, the smell of freshly roasted coffee hits you. Inside, nothing matches. The wooden tables and chairs all look like they came from different flea markets, and there are hanging plants everywhere, so it almost feels like a greenhouse. My favorite seat is by the big window, where I can look down at the busy street while everything inside stays calm. The owner plays old jazz records and remembers every regular's order. Honestly, it feels more like visiting a friend's apartment than going to a café.

The café I'd like to talk about is the one in my neighborhood, about a five-minute walk from my apartment, and I spend most of my Saturday mornings there. It's a small place, but the front wall is made entirely of glass, so it's always bright and airy, even in winter. On one side, there are a few soft, deep sofas that are perfect for reading, and in the back there's a long communal table where students and freelancers work quietly on their laptops. The owner bakes all the cakes and scones herself early in the morning, so the whole café smells like butter and cinnamon when it opens. What really makes it special, though, is the feeling of the place. The music is low, people speak softly, and nobody ever makes you feel like you've stayed too long. That's why I keep going back almost every week.

questions.question: What do you usually do when you go to a café? When do you go, who do you go with, and what do you usually order? Walk me through a typical visit.

il.text: I go to a café on Sunday afternoon. I usually go alone. I order an iced latte. I read a book or study English. I stay for two hours. It is my favorite time of the week.
I go to a café with my friends after work. We go on Friday. I order a hot americano and a piece of cake. We talk about our week. We laugh a lot. It is very fun.

im1.text: I usually go to a café on Sunday afternoons, and I go by myself. When I get there, I order an iced latte and sometimes a small cookie. Then I find a seat by the window. First, I read a book for about an hour. After that, I study English or plan my week in my notebook. I usually stay for two or three hours. It is quiet time for me, and I really need it.

I go to a café with my coworkers almost every day after lunch. It is right next to our office building. I always order a hot americano because it is cheap and it helps me wake up. My coworkers usually get lattes. We sit together for about twenty minutes and talk about work or our weekend plans. Then we go back to the office. It is a short but important break for us.
phrases: It is a short but important break

im2.text: On Sunday afternoons, I usually go to a café by myself. I leave home around two, and it takes about ten minutes to walk there. I almost always order an iced latte, and if I'm hungry, I get a cookie too. Then I look for a seat by the window, because I like the natural light. For the first hour, I read a book. After that, I study English or write my plans for the next week in my notebook. I usually stay for about three hours. It's my way of getting ready for a busy week.

I go to a café with my coworkers almost every weekday after lunch. There's a small café right next to our office, so it's very convenient. I usually order a hot americano because I need the caffeine to stay awake in the afternoon. My coworkers usually get lattes or tea. We sit at the same table by the door every day, and we chat for about twenty minutes. We talk about work, our weekend plans, or funny things that happened. Then we go back to the office. This short break helps me relax and focus again.
phrases: There's a small café right next to

im3.text: My café routine is pretty much the same every Sunday. Around two in the afternoon, I grab my bag with a book and my notebook and walk to the café near my house. I almost always order an iced latte, even in winter, and sometimes a chocolate chip cookie if they have fresh ones. Then I try to get the window seat, because the sunlight makes me feel calm. I spend the first hour reading, and after that I switch to studying English or planning my week. I usually stay until about five. By the time I leave, I feel organized and ready for Monday, so I really look forward to it.

On weekdays, going to the café with my coworkers after lunch is kind of a ritual. Right after we finish eating, the four of us walk to the small café next to our building. I always order a hot americano, no matter the weather, because otherwise I get really sleepy at around three. The others usually get lattes, and one of them always tries the new seasonal drink. We grab the same table near the door and chat for about twenty minutes. Honestly, it's the only time we talk about things other than work. That little break makes the afternoon go much faster. We even celebrate birthdays there with a small cake sometimes.

questions.question: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a café. When did it happen, who were you with, and what exactly happened? Please describe it in detail.

il.text: Last year, I met my old friend at a café. I did not see her for five years. We were very happy. We talked for four hours. We forgot the time. The café closed, so we left. It was a great day.
One day, I spilled coffee at a café. It was on my laptop. I was very surprised. The staff helped me. They gave me many napkins. My laptop was okay. I was lucky.

im1.text: I remember a special day last year. I met my high school friend at a café. We had not seen each other for five years because she lived in another country. When I saw her, I was so happy that I almost cried. We ordered coffee and cake, and we talked about everything. We talked for about four hours. Finally, the staff told us the café was closing. It was one of the best days of my year.
phrases: We had not seen each other

im1.text: About two years ago, I had a funny accident at a café. I was working on my laptop, and I had a big iced coffee next to it. When I reached for my phone, I knocked the cup over. The coffee went all over my laptop and my notes. I was really shocked. Luckily, the staff ran over with lots of napkins and helped me clean up. My laptop still worked, so I was very relieved.

im2.text: One of my most memorable café experiences happened last spring. My best friend from high school came back to Korea after living abroad for five years, and we decided to meet at a café near my house. When she walked in, I recognized her right away, and we both screamed a little. We ordered coffee and a big piece of cheesecake, but we were so busy talking that we forgot to eat it. We talked about our jobs, our families, and our old school memories. Before we knew it, four hours had passed and the café was closing. I'll never forget that day.
phrases: One of my most memorable café experiences

im2.text: A memorable thing happened to me at a café about two years ago. I was preparing for an important presentation, so I was working on my laptop with a large iced coffee next to it. When I reached for my phone, I accidentally knocked the cup over, and the coffee spilled all over my keyboard and my notes. I panicked because my presentation was the next morning. Fortunately, the staff came over quickly with towels and helped me dry everything. My laptop survived, and the presentation went well. Since then, I never put drinks next to my laptop.
phrases: A memorable thing happened to me

im3.text: The café experience I remember best was last spring, when my best friend from high school came back to Korea. Before we realized it, four hours had gone by, and the staff had started stacking the chairs. It felt like no time had passed between us.

Thankfully, two staff members rushed over with towels, turned my laptop upside down, and helped me dry it. Amazingly, it still worked, and my presentation the next day went fine.

questions.question: Cafés have changed a lot over the years. How are the cafés you go to now different from cafés you remember from the past? How have the way people use cafés and what they order changed?

il.text: In the past, cafés were small. People just drank coffee and talked. Now, cafés are big and pretty. Many people study or work there. There are many kinds of drinks now. I like cafés now more.
phrases: Many people study or work there

il.text: Ten years ago, there were not many cafés. Coffee was cheap. Now there are cafés everywhere. Coffee is more expensive. People take many pictures in cafés now. It is very different.

im1.text: Cafés are very different now. When I was in high school, cafés were small and a little dark, and people went there just to meet friends and drink coffee. These days, cafés are big, bright, and beautiful. Many people go there alone to study or work on their laptops. Also, menus are different. In the past, there were only a few kinds of coffee, but now there are many special drinks and desserts. I think cafés are more fun now.

I think the biggest change is the number of cafés. About ten years ago, there were only a few cafés in my neighborhood. Now, there are cafés on almost every street. Another change is the price. Coffee was cheaper before, but now a latte is quite expensive. Also, people use cafés differently. In the past, people just talked, but now many people take pictures of their drinks and post them online.
phrases: I think the biggest change is
In the past, people just talked

im2.text: Cafés have changed a lot since I was a teenager. Back then, most cafés were small, a little dark, and pretty simple. People went there mainly to meet friends and have a conversation. Nowadays, cafés are much bigger and brighter, and many of them have unique interior designs. The biggest difference is how people use them. A lot of people go to cafés alone to study, work on their laptops, or even have online meetings. The menus have changed too. In the past, there were only a few basic coffees, but now there are dozens of drinks and fancy desserts.

When I compare cafés now with cafés ten years ago, I notice three big changes. First, there are so many more cafés. In my neighborhood, there used to be only two or three, but now there's one on almost every corner. Second, coffee has become much more expensive, and some drinks cost almost as much as a meal. Third, people use cafés in different ways. In the past, people mostly sat and talked, but now many people take photos of their drinks for social media or spend the whole day studying. I think cafés have become part of daily life.
phrases: have become part of daily life

im3.text: Cafés today are really different from the ones I remember from my teenage years. Back then, cafés were mostly small, slightly dark places with simple furniture, and people went there for one reason, to meet friends and chat over coffee. Nowadays, cafés compete with each other on design. Some look like art galleries, and others are full of plants or have rooftop terraces. The biggest change, though, is how people use them. Many people go alone and stay for hours, studying, working on laptops, or even joining video meetings. The menu has also exploded. Instead of a few basic coffees, there are seasonal drinks, plant-based milk options, and desserts that look like works of art.
phrases: compete with each other on design

ih.text: When I think about how cafés have changed over the last ten years, three things come to mind right away. The first is simply the number of them. When I was in high school, there were maybe two cafés in my whole neighborhood, and now it feels like there's one on every corner, sometimes two right next to each other. The second is the price. A latte used to be a cheap little treat, but these days some specialty drinks cost almost as much as a full lunch, which still surprises me. al.text: Honestly, the cafés I go to now are almost unrecognizable compared to the ones I remember from my teenage years. Back then, a typical café was small and a bit dim, with plain wooden chairs, a few old posters, and a short menu handwritten on a board behind the counter. People went there for pretty much one purpose, which was to sit with friends and talk for an hour or so. Today, cafés seem to compete with each other mainly on design and atmosphere. Some look like minimalist art galleries, others are practically indoor jungles, and the trendier ones have rooftop terraces with views of the whole city. However, what's changed the most, in my view, is the way people actually use these spaces. It's perfectly normal now to see someone sitting alone for five hours, working on a laptop, studying for an exam, or even leading a video meeting with headphones on. The menus have evolved just as dramatically. Instead of a handful of basic coffees, you'll find seasonal specials, several kinds of plant-based milk, and desserts so elaborate that people photograph them from every angle before taking a single bite.
phrases: compete with each other mainly on
However, what's changed the most, in my view

al.text: Looking at how cafés have evolved over the past decade, I'd point to three major changes. The first is sheer quantity. When I was in high school, my neighborhood had maybe two cafés in total, whereas now it feels like there's one on every corner, and sometimes two competing ones right across the street from each other. The second change is price. A latte used to be an affordable little treat, but nowadays some specialty drinks cost nearly as much as a decent lunch, which I still find a bit hard to accept. The third change, and probably the most significant, is the role cafés play in everyday life. In the past, people would drop in for an hour to catch up with a friend and then leave. These days, cafés have become multipurpose spaces. They serve as offices for freelancers, study rooms for students, and even photo studios for people who mainly come to take pictures for social media. To be honest, I have mixed feelings about it, because cafés feel less social than before. Still, I'd be lying if I said I didn't spend whole Saturdays working in one myself.
