While the coffee is brewing, I make my bed and open the windows to let in fresh air. After work, I get home around seven in the evening. First, I change my clothes and cook dinner. Since I live with my parents, we divide the chores. My mom does most of the cooking, my dad takes care of the laundry, and I vacuum the whole apartment every other day. It works pretty well for us.
phrases: my weekday routine is pretty simple
It works pretty well for us

im2.text: Okay. Because I live alone, I have to do everything by myself, so I try to keep a regular routine. In the morning, I get up at six thirty, do some quick exercises, and eat a bowl of rice with eggs. In the evening, I usually spend about thirty minutes cleaning. On Mondays I do the laundry, on Wednesdays I clean the bathroom, and on Fridays I vacuum. After that, I relax on the sofa and watch a show. Doing a little every day is much easier than cleaning everything on the weekend.
phrases: I have to do everything by myself

im3.text: Sure. On a typical weekday, I get up around six forty-five, and the first thing I do is open the curtains and turn on some music. Then I take a quick shower, make a smoothie, and leave for work by seven thirty. Evenings are a little more relaxed. I live with two roommates, and we have a simple rule for chores. Whoever cooks doesn't have to wash the dishes. So if I cook, one of my roommates cleans up, and the other one takes out the trash. On top of that, we do a big cleaning together every Sunday. It sounds strict, but honestly, it has really reduced the arguments in our home.
phrases: the first thing I do is
we have a simple rule for chores

im3.text: Let me walk you through a normal weekday. Since I work from home three days a week, my routine changes a little depending on the day. On home days, I wake up at eight, make coffee, and start working at my desk in the living room. At lunchtime, I usually cook something simple and take a short walk around the block. In the evening, I share the chores with my husband. He's a much better cook than I am, so he makes dinner, and I wash the dishes and clean the kitchen. Before going to bed, we usually spend some time on the sofa talking about our day, which is my favorite part of the routine.
phrases: He's a much better cook than I am

ih.text: Sure. My weekday routine at home is pretty structured, mostly because I have two kids. I wake up at six, before anyone else, and I really treasure that quiet half hour with a cup of coffee. Then the chaos begins. I wake the kids up, make breakfast, and get them ready for school while my husband packs their lunches. In the evening, after dinner, we have a rule that everyone in the family has to do at least one chore. The kids set the table and fold the laundry, my husband washes the dishes, and I usually wipe down the kitchen and take out the recycling. It took a while to get everyone used to it, but now it runs pretty smoothly, and the kids actually seem proud of helping out. Before bed, we all read together for twenty minutes, and that's the calmest part of our day.
phrases: It took a while to get everyone used to it

ih.text: Okay, so my weekdays at home are pretty predictable. I live alone, and I've found that having a routine is the only way to keep my apartment from turning into a mess. In the morning, I get up at seven, make my bed right away, and have a light breakfast while I check the news. I leave for work at eight. When I get home around seven, I don't let myself sit on the sofa right away, because I know I'll never get up again. Instead, I spend fifteen minutes doing one small chore, like cleaning the bathroom sink or sorting the laundry. After that, I cook dinner, usually something quick like pasta or stir-fried vegetables. Later in the evening, I read or watch a documentary, and I try to be in bed by eleven thirty. It's a simple routine, but it keeps me sane.

al.text: Sure. On a typical weekday, my routine at home revolves around the fact that I share a small apartment with two roommates who all have very different schedules. I'm usually the first one up, around six thirty, so I try to be as quiet as possible while I make coffee and get ready. One of my roommates works night shifts at a hospital, so she's often coming home just as I'm leaving. Because our schedules overlap so little, we figured out pretty early on that we needed a clear system for chores. We have a shared calendar on our phones, and each week the tasks rotate, so one person handles the kitchen, another takes care of the bathroom, and the third deals with the trash and recycling. In the evenings, if I'm on kitchen duty, I'll clean up after dinner and wipe everything down before bed. Honestly, it isn't always perfect, and occasionally someone forgets their turn, but compared to my first year of living with roommates, when there was no system at all, it's a huge improvement.
phrases: we figured out pretty early on that

al.text: Of course. These days, my weekday routine at home is shaped by the fact that I live with my elderly parents. I usually wake up at six, and before I do anything else, I make breakfast for the three of us, usually rice, soup, and a few side dishes. My mom used to do all of the cooking, but since she hurt her back last year, I've taken over most of the kitchen work. After breakfast, I make sure my dad has taken his medicine, and then I head to the office. In the evening, my brother sometimes comes over to help, which makes a big difference. He takes care of the heavier chores, like carrying groceries and taking out the trash, while I do the laundry and clean the bathroom. It can be exhausting, and there are days when I'd love to just collapse on the sofa. But I've come to appreciate this time with my parents, because I know that a few years from now, I'll probably look back on it and miss it.
phrases: is shaped by the fact that

questions.tip_ko: 아침 → 저녁 순서로 시간 표현(First, After that, Before bed)을 넣어요. 집안일은 누가 무엇을 맡는지 이름 대신 관계로 말하면 돼요.

questions.question: Think about a memorable experience you had at home. Maybe you moved into a new place, or something went wrong in your home. What happened, and how did you deal with it? Please tell me the whole story in detail.

il.text: Last year, I moved to a new apartment. My friends helped me. We carried many boxes. It was very hot. After that, we ate pizza together. I was tired but happy. It was a good day.
One night, the power went out in my house. It was very dark. I could not see anything. I found a candle. I waited for one hour. Then the light came back. I was scared.

im1.text: Two years ago, I moved out of my parents' house for the first time. I found a small apartment near my company. On moving day, it rained a lot, so my boxes got wet. My dad helped me carry everything. That night, I sat in my empty room and ate instant noodles. I felt a little lonely, but I was also excited. It was the start of my new life.
phrases: I felt a little lonely, but

im1.text: Last winter, a pipe in our kitchen broke. Water came out everywhere, and the floor was wet. I didn't know what to do, so I called my landlord. He sent a repairman, but he came three hours later. While I waited, I cleaned the water with towels. It was really stressful. After that day, I learned where the main water valve is.
phrases: I didn't know what to do

im2.text: I remember the day we moved into our current apartment. I was about fifteen years old. We had a lot of furniture, so the moving company came early in the morning. Everything went well until they tried to bring our big sofa through the front door. It didn't fit! We tried for almost an hour, and finally they had to lift it through the balcony window with a special machine. All the neighbors came out to watch. At that time, I was embarrassed, but now my family laughs about it every time we sit on that sofa.
phrases: now my family laughs about it

im2.text: One memorable experience happened last summer. I was living with two roommates, and one night the air conditioner suddenly stopped working. It was over thirty degrees, so none of us could sleep. We opened all the windows, but it didn't help. The next morning, we called the repair center, but they said they couldn't come for a week. So we went out and bought three fans and slept in the living room together like a camping trip. It was uncomfortable, but we talked until late, and it actually became a fun memory.
phrases: it actually became a fun memory

im3.text: Sure. A few years ago, I had a pretty scary experience at home. I was living alone at the time, and one night, I came home from work and noticed that my front door was slightly open. I was sure I had locked it in the morning, so I panicked. I didn't go inside. Instead, I called the building manager, and we went in together. It turned out that nothing was missing, and the lock was just broken. The manager replaced it the next day, but for about a week, I couldn't sleep well. Since then, I always check the lock twice before I leave, even when I'm in a hurry.

Let me tell you about the time I moved into my first apartment with a roommate. We were both college students, and we didn't have much money, so we decided to move everything ourselves. We borrowed a small truck from my uncle, and it took us four trips to carry all our stuff. On the last trip, we realized we had forgotten the keys to the new apartment at the old place! We had to drive all the way back in the rain. By the time we finally finished, it was almost midnight. We were exhausted, but we ordered fried chicken and celebrated on the floor of our empty living room.
phrases: Let me tell you about the time
By the time we finally finished

ih.text: Okay, one experience that really stands out happened about three years ago, right after I moved into my current apartment. It was my first winter there, and one morning I woke up and the whole place was freezing. I checked the heater, and it wasn't working at all. I called the landlord, but he was on vacation and didn't answer, so I had to find a repair company on my own. The first company said they couldn't come for four days, which was obviously not an option. Finally, a small local shop agreed to come that afternoon. The repairman found out that a part had frozen and cracked, and it took him almost three hours to fix it. In the meantime, I wrapped myself in every blanket I had. Looking back, it was a stressful day, but it taught me to always keep the landlord's backup number and to check the heating system before winter starts.
phrases: one experience that really stands out
which was obviously not an option

ih.text: Sure. I'd say the most memorable thing that happened at home was when my family decided to remodel our kitchen while we were still living in the house. I was in high school at the time, and my parents thought it would only take two weeks. Well, it ended up taking almost two months. For the first few days, it was kind of fun. We ate takeout every night and had picnics on the living room floor. But after a while, everyone got really tired of the dust and the noise. Then one day, the workers accidentally hit a water pipe, and water flooded part of the living room. My mom was so upset that she almost cried. In the end, the kitchen turned out beautifully, and we still use it every day, but whenever someone in my family mentions remodeling, we all just laugh and shake our heads.
phrases: I'd say the most memorable thing

al.text: Sure. The experience that comes to mind right away is the time I moved out of my parents' house to live on my own for the first time. I was twenty-four and had just started my first full-time job, and I was incredibly excited about the idea of having my own place. I spent weeks looking at apartments, and I finally found a small one about twenty minutes from my office. The moving day itself was a bit of a disaster. The moving truck showed up two hours late, it started pouring rain halfway through, and one of the movers dropped a box full of my favorite mugs. By the time everyone left, my apartment was a maze of wet boxes, and I couldn't even find my towels. I remember sitting on the floor, eating cold kimbap from a convenience store, and wondering why I had wanted to leave home so badly. But a few days later, after I unpacked and arranged everything the way I liked, I started to feel genuinely proud. Looking back, that rough first night was actually the beginning of me becoming more independent.
phrases: The experience that comes to mind right away
was a bit of a disaster

al.text: Of course. One experience I'll never forget happened a couple of summers ago, when I was living with two roommates in an old apartment. We'd been having small problems with the plumbing for months, but our landlord kept putting off the repairs. Then one Saturday morning, I woke up to the sound of water dripping, and when I walked into the bathroom, there was water pouring out from behind the toilet. Within minutes, it had spread into the hallway. None of us knew where the main valve was, so we were running around grabbing towels and buckets while one of my roommates searched online for instructions. Eventually, we found the valve in a cabinet under the kitchen sink and managed to turn it off. The landlord finally came that afternoon, and to his credit, he paid for everything, including a new hallway carpet. Even though it was chaotic at the time, it brought the three of us closer together, and it taught me to always find out exactly where the shutoff valve is whenever I move into a new place.
phrases: Even though it was chaotic at the time

questions.tip_ko: 언제, 어디서, 무슨 일이 → 어떻게 해결했는지 → 지금 드는 생각 순서로 과거형을 지켜 말해요. 그때 느낀 감정을 한 문장 넣어요.

questions.question: Compare the home you live in now with the home you lived in when you were a child. How are they different? What has changed, and which home do you like better? Please explain in detail.

il.text: When I was a child, I lived in a small house. Now I live in an apartment. My old house had a yard. My apartment has no yard. But my apartment is warm and clean. I like my apartment more.
My old home was in the country. It was big and quiet. Now my home is in the city. It is small and busy. I miss my old home. But the city is convenient.

im1.text: When I was a child, I lived in a house in a small town with my grandparents. It had a big garden, and we grew vegetables there. Now I live in an apartment in Seoul. It is much smaller, and there is no garden. But it is very convenient because there are many stores and a subway station nearby. I think my old house was more peaceful, but my apartment is better for my life now.
phrases: but my apartment is better for

im1.text: My childhood home was an old apartment with only two rooms. I shared a room with my brother, so I had no privacy. Now I live alone in a studio, so I have my own space. My current home is newer and has a nice kitchen. However, my old home was always full of people and laughter. Sometimes I miss that feeling, but I like my freedom now.

im2.text: I grew up in a traditional house with a small yard in a quiet neighborhood. In winter, the house was really cold because it was old, and we used a heater in only one room. Now I live in a modern apartment with my roommates. It has central heating, so it's warm everywhere, and there's an elevator and a security guard. The biggest change is convenience. Everything is easier now. On the other hand, I miss playing in the yard and seeing the stars at night. Overall, I prefer my current home, but my childhood home has more memories.

When I was young, my family lived in a big apartment in the suburbs. We had four bedrooms, so everyone had their own room. Now I live with my husband in a small apartment downtown. It's only half the size of my childhood home, but it's close to our offices, so we save a lot of time. Another difference is the neighbors. In my old apartment, we knew everyone in the building. Now I don't even know who lives next door. I like my current home, but I think people were closer back then.

im3.text: The home I live in now is really different from the one I grew up in. When I was a kid, my family lived in a two-story house in a small city. There was a big yard, and my dad built a little wooden swing for me and my sister. Now I live alone in a one-room apartment in Seoul. Of course, it's much smaller, and I can't have a yard or even a pet. But it has some advantages. Everything is close, the building is safe, and I don't have to spend hours cleaning a big house. If I'm honest, I think I prefer my current place for now, but when I have my own family someday, I'd like to live in a house like the one I grew up in.

Let me compare the two. As a child, I lived in a crowded apartment with my parents, my grandmother, and two brothers. There was only one bathroom, so every morning was like a battle. Now I share a newer apartment with just one roommate, and we each have our own bathroom, which honestly feels like luxury. The atmosphere has changed, too. My childhood home was always noisy and warm, and someone was always cooking. My current home is quiet and calm, which is great when I need to focus, but sometimes it feels a bit empty. So I'd say each home suits a different stage of my life, and I'm thankful for both of them.

ih.text: Sure. The biggest difference between my childhood home and my current one is probably the sense of space. I grew up in a farmhouse in the countryside, surrounded by rice fields. We had a huge yard, a small barn, and so much room that I could ride my bike around the house. Now I live with my wife in a two-bedroom apartment on the fifteenth floor of a high-rise in the city. When we first moved in, I honestly felt a little trapped, because I was used to stepping outside and seeing open land. Over time, though, I've gotten used to it, and I've come to appreciate how convenient city life is. We can walk to the subway, the hospital, and the grocery store in ten minutes. Still, if you asked me which one I like better, I'd say my childhood home. Whenever I visit my parents and smell the fields, I realize how much I miss that freedom.
phrases: Over time, though, I've gotten used to it
if you asked me which one

ih.text: Okay. When I think about it, my current home and the one I grew up in reflect how much my life has changed. As a kid, I lived in a small rented apartment with my mom, and we moved almost every two years because the rent kept going up. Because of that, I never really decorated my room or felt settled. These days, I live in an apartment that my husband and I bought three years ago, and it's the first place that truly feels like ours. We painted the walls, chose our own furniture, and even turned one room into a little library. The funny thing is that my current home is not much bigger than my childhood apartment. The difference is the feeling of stability. So while I have some sweet memories of my old home, especially cooking with my mom in that tiny kitchen, I definitely prefer where I live now.

al.text: That's an interesting question, because my current home and my childhood home are almost complete opposites. I grew up in a big, old house in a coastal town, with high ceilings, creaky wooden floors, and a garden my grandmother took care of every single day. It was drafty in the winter and full of bugs in the summer, but it had so much character, and there was always something going on. Today, I live alone in a brand-new studio apartment in the middle of the city. Everything is efficient and modern. The heating is automatic, the doors lock with a code, and I can order groceries without leaving my sofa. In terms of comfort and convenience, there's really no comparison; my current place wins easily. However, I've noticed that I spend a lot less time at home now. My apartment feels more like a place to sleep than a place to live. So if I had to choose, I'd probably pick my childhood home, not because it was nicer, but because it was full of people and stories, and that's what made it feel like a real home.
phrases: In terms of comfort and convenience
not because it was nicer, but because

al.text: Sure. I'd say the main difference between the home I grew up in and the one I live in now isn't really the building itself, but the people and the routines inside it. As a child, I lived in a fairly ordinary apartment with my parents and my younger sister. It wasn't big or fancy, but my parents were very strict about family time, so we always had dinner together and spent Sunday afternoons cleaning the whole place as a team. Now I share a bigger and much nicer apartment with two coworkers. We each have our own bedroom and bathroom, and the kitchen is twice the size of my parents' kitchen. On paper, it's a better home in almost every way. But because all three of us work long hours, we rarely eat together, and the living room is often empty. Honestly, living here has made me appreciate my childhood home a lot more. If I could combine the space of my current apartment with the warmth of the place I grew up in, I think that would be my ideal home.
phrases: isn't really the building itself, but

questions.tip_ko: 어릴 때 집과 지금 집을 크기·위치·분위기처럼 기준 두세 개로 나눠 비교해요. 마지막에 어느 쪽이 더 좋은지와 이유로 마무리해요.

questions.question: You indicated in the survey that you enjoy watching movies. What kind of movies do you like the most? Tell me about your favorite type of movie and why you like it.

il.text: I like comedy movies. They are funny. I watch them on the weekend. I laugh a lot. Comedy movies make me happy. I usually watch them with my sister. They are not long or difficult, so I like them.
My favorite movies are action movies. There are many fights and car chases. They are exciting. I like the music too. I watch action movies at home or at the theater. They are really fun for me.

im1.text: I really like comedy movies. When I watch a comedy, I can forget about my stress. I usually watch them on Friday night after work. My favorite kind is a family comedy, because the stories are simple and warm. Sometimes I watch them with my sister, and we laugh together. I don't like scary movies, because I can't sleep after watching them. So comedy is the best for me.

My favorite type of movie is action. I like action movies because they are exciting and fast. There are a lot of fights, explosions and car chases. I think the special effects are really cool. I usually go to the theater to watch them, because the big screen and loud sound make them more exciting. I watch about two action movies every month, usually with my friends.
phrases: My favorite type of movie is

im2.text: Well, I watch many kinds of movies, but my favorite type is comedy. There are a few reasons. First, comedy movies help me relax. My job is pretty stressful, so on Friday nights I just want to laugh and forget about work. Second, comedies are easy to enjoy with other people. I often watch them with my family, and everyone can understand the story. For example, last weekend we watched a comedy about a clumsy dog, and my parents laughed the whole time. So that's why I love comedy movies.

My favorite type of movie is science fiction. I like sci-fi movies because they show a world that doesn't exist yet, like life in space or robots that can think. When I watch them, I start imagining the future, and that's really exciting for me. I usually watch these movies at the theater, because the visual effects look amazing on a big screen. After the movie, I like talking about the story with my friends over coffee. These movies also make me curious about science and technology. That's why sci-fi is my favorite kind of movie.

im3.text: Actually, I enjoy almost every kind of movie, but if I had to pick one, I'd say thrillers. What I like most about thrillers is the tension. From the beginning, the story keeps me guessing, and I can never really relax until the end. I also like trying to figure out who the bad guy is before the movie tells me. Sometimes I guess right, and I feel really proud of myself. I usually watch thrillers at home at night with the lights off, because it makes the mood more intense. My friends say thrillers are too stressful, but for me, that's exactly the fun part. So thrillers are definitely my favorite.
phrases: if I had to pick one

im3.text: My favorite type of movie is animation. Some people think animated movies are only for kids, but I don't agree at all. Many animated movies have really deep stories about family, friendship, and growing up. I remember crying at the end of one about an old man and a little boy who went on an adventure together. Also, the colors and the drawings are just beautiful, so it feels like watching a moving painting. In my opinion, some of them are even better than regular movies. These days I watch an animated movie almost every weekend, usually on my laptop in bed. It's a perfect way to end a long week, and I always feel warm afterward.

ih.text: I'd say my favorite kind of movie is the historical drama. I've always been interested in history, and these movies make the past feel real in a way that textbooks never could. What I love most is the detail, like the costumes, the old buildings, and the way people talked back then. When I watch one, I feel like I'm traveling back in time. Usually, after the movie ends, I look up the real events online to see how accurate the story was. Sometimes I find out the director changed quite a lot, which is interesting too. I prefer watching these movies at a theater, because the big screen really shows off the scenery and the battle scenes. Honestly, historical dramas are long, often more than two and a half hours, but I never get bored. They're the kind of movies I keep thinking about for days.

To be honest, my favorite type of movie is the romantic comedy, even though some of my friends tease me about it. I know the stories are usually predictable. Two people meet, they don't like each other at first, and then they slowly fall in love. But I think that's exactly why I enjoy them. After a long, tiring week, I don't want to think too hard. I just want something light and sweet that makes me smile. I also like the dialogue in good romantic comedies, because the characters are often really witty. I usually watch them on Sunday evenings at home with a bowl of popcorn and a blanket. Recently, I've started watching some older ones from the nineties, and I was surprised by how well they still hold up. So yes, they might be a little cheesy, but they always put me in a good mood.
phrases: put me in a good mood

al.text: If I had to choose just one genre, I'd go with documentaries, which might sound a little unusual for a movie lover. The thing is, I've always been the kind of person who gets curious about how things work, and documentaries feed that curiosity better than anything else. I especially like nature documentaries and the ones about how ordinary people live in different parts of the world. A good documentary doesn't just give you information. It tells a story, and you end up caring about the people or animals on the screen. I remember watching one about a small fishing village where the young people were all moving to the city. By the end, I felt like I knew the families personally, and it made me think about my own grandparents' hometown. I usually watch documentaries alone, late at night, because I like to focus completely. Afterward, I often end up reading more about the topic for an hour or two. In that sense, a documentary is not just entertainment for me. It's a starting point for learning something new.
phrases: If I had to choose just one

al.text: My favorite kind of movie would have to be the independent film, the small, low-budget movies that don't usually get shown in big theaters. I started getting into them in university, when a friend took me to a little film festival downtown, and honestly, it completely changed the way I think about movies. Big blockbusters are fun, but they tend to follow the same formula. Independent films, on the other hand, take risks. The stories are often about very ordinary people, and the endings aren't always happy, which actually makes them feel more honest. I also love that the actors are usually people I've never seen before, so I don't have any expectations. These days, I try to watch at least two or three independent films a month, either at a small art theater near my office or online. What I enjoy most is discussing them afterward, because everyone seems to notice something different. If a movie leaves me thinking about it the next morning, I know it was worth watching.

questions.tip_ko: 장르 하나를 고르고 좋아하는 이유를 두 가지 말해요. 기억나는 영화 장면 하나를 덧붙이면 답이 자연스럽게 길어져요.

questions.question: Tell me about what you usually do when you go to see a movie. What do you do before the movie starts, and what do you usually do after it ends? Please describe your routine in detail.

il.text: I go to the movies on Saturday. First, I buy a ticket online. Then I buy popcorn and a coke. I watch the movie. After the movie, I eat dinner with my friend. Then I go home.
I usually go to the theater with my brother. We meet at the station. We buy snacks. Then we watch the movie. After that, we talk about the movie. It is fun. Then we go home by bus.

im1.text: When I go to the movies, I usually go on Saturday afternoon. First, I check the movie times on my phone and buy a ticket online. I like to arrive about twenty minutes early. Before the movie starts, I buy popcorn and a soda. I always choose a seat in the middle. After the movie, I usually go to a restaurant with my friend, and we talk about the story. Then I go home.

I usually go to the theater once or twice a month with my girlfriend. Before the movie, we have a quick dinner near the theater. Then we buy one big popcorn to share. During the movie, I turn off my phone, because I don't want to bother other people. When the movie ends, we walk around the shopping mall and talk about our favorite scenes. It's our regular date course.

im2.text: My movie routine is pretty simple. Before I go, I usually read a few reviews online, but I try not to read too much, because I don't want any spoilers. I book my ticket a day early so I can get a good seat in the middle. On the day of the movie, I get to the theater about fifteen minutes early and buy a big bucket of popcorn. I always turn off my phone before the movie starts. After the movie, my friends and I go to a café nearby and talk about the ending. That's usually the best part of the day.
phrases: My movie routine is pretty simple

im2.text: When I watch a movie at the theater, I usually follow the same steps. First, I choose the movie with my friends in our group chat. Then I book the tickets online, because the good seats sell out fast on weekends. Before the movie, we meet in front of the theater and buy snacks. I usually get nachos instead of popcorn. During the movie, I try to stay quiet and focus. When it's over, we rate the movie from one to ten and share our scores. It sounds a little silly, but we always have fun doing it.
phrases: I usually follow the same steps

im3.text: Going to the movies is kind of a ritual for me. A few days before, I watch the trailer again to get excited, and I book my ticket online so I can choose the perfect seat, usually a few rows from the back in the center. On the day, I try to have a light meal first, because I don't like eating too much during the movie. I still buy a small popcorn, though, because a movie without popcorn feels strange to me. Once the lights go down, I put my phone in my bag so I'm not tempted to check it. After the movie, I usually stay in my seat until the end credits finish, because sometimes there's a hidden scene. Then I head home and read what other people thought about it online.
phrases: is kind of a ritual for me

im3.text: My routine depends on who I'm going with, but usually I go with my two closest friends from work. We normally pick a late show on Friday, around nine o'clock, so we have time to eat dinner first. We always go to the same Korean restaurant across from the theater, and that's when we argue about what to expect from the movie. Before going in, we each buy a drink, but we share one large popcorn. During the movie, nobody is allowed to talk, which is our strict rule. Afterward, since it's usually late, we just walk to the station together and share our opinions on the way. By the time I get home, it's almost midnight, but it's a great way to finish the week.

ih.text: I go to the movies about twice a month, and over time I've developed a pretty fixed routine. It starts a couple of days before, when I check which movies are showing and read a few short reviews, just enough to know if it's worth it. Then I book a seat online. I'm a little picky about seats, so I always choose one in the center, about two-thirds of the way back, where the sound is best. On the day, I arrive around twenty minutes early, which gives me time to grab popcorn and use the restroom so I don't have to leave in the middle. Once the movie starts, my phone goes on silent and into my pocket. After it ends, I usually stay through the credits, partly to look for a bonus scene and partly just to let the story sink in. Then, if I'm with friends, we grab a late snack and talk it over. If I'm alone, I write a short review in a note app on my phone.

My movie routine has actually changed a bit since I started working, but these days it goes something like this. I usually go to an early morning showing on Sunday, because the tickets are cheaper and the theater is almost empty. The night before, I pick the movie and book my ticket, so I don't have to rush in the morning. I wake up around eight, grab a coffee at a café near the theater, and get there about ten minutes before it starts. I skip the popcorn in the morning, which probably sounds strange, but coffee is enough for me. Watching a movie in an empty theater feels almost like having a private screening, and I can really concentrate. When it's over, I take a slow walk home along the river, thinking about the story. By noon, I'm back home, and I still have the whole afternoon free.
phrases: has actually changed a bit since

al.text: For me, going to the movies is less about the movie itself and more about the whole experience, so I've ended up with a routine I hardly ever break. It begins a few days in advance. I'll watch the trailer, maybe read one or two reviews from critics I trust, and then reserve a seat. I'm pretty particular about where I sit, so I always book the center of the row, roughly two-thirds of the way back, where the screen fills your view without hurting your neck. On the day itself, I try to arrive early enough to pick up a drink and a small popcorn without feeling rushed, because nothing ruins the mood like running in after the opening scene. Once the lights dim, my phone goes completely off, not just on silent. When the movie ends, I almost always stay until the very last credit rolls. It gives me a few quiet minutes to process what I've just seen. After that, I'll usually meet up with a friend for a drink and argue about the ending, which, to be honest, is sometimes more fun than the movie itself.

Since I became a parent, my movie routine has completely changed, so I'll describe what it looks like now. My wife and I only get to go to the theater about once a month, when my mother offers to babysit, so we really try to make it special. A week before, we sit down together and choose a movie, which usually involves a lot of negotiating, because she loves dramas and I'd rather see something with action. Once we agree, I book two seats for an evening show. On the day, we drop our son off at my mother's place, and then we have dinner at a restaurant near the theater. It's one of the few times we can actually talk without being interrupted. At the theater, we share a large popcorn and a drink, and we both switch our phones to vibrate, just in case my mother calls. After the movie, we don't hurry home. We usually take a short walk and talk about the story, and it honestly feels like we're dating again. It's a small routine, but it means a lot to us.
phrases: so I'll describe what it looks like now
it means a lot to us

questions.tip_ko: 영화 보기 전, 보는 중, 본 뒤로 나눠 순서대로 말해요. First, Before, After 같은 연결어를 쓰면 흐름이 분명해져요.

questions.question: Think about a movie-watching experience that you still remember well. When was it, who were you with, and what happened? Tell me the whole story and why it was so memorable.

il.text: Last year, I watched a movie with my father. It was an action movie. The theater was very big. The sound was loud. My father liked the movie. I was happy. We ate dinner after the movie.
I remember my first movie in a theater. I was seven years old. I went with my mom. It was a cartoon movie. I ate popcorn. I was very excited. It was a good day.

im1.text: I remember the first time I watched a movie alone. It was two years ago, on my birthday. My friends were all busy, so I went to the theater by myself. At first, I felt a little strange. But the movie was a funny comedy, and I laughed a lot. After the movie, I felt really free and happy. Now I like watching movies alone sometimes.

Last summer, I watched a horror movie with my friends. It was a very scary movie about a haunted house. In the middle of the movie, my friend screamed very loudly, and everyone in the theater looked at us. We were so embarrassed. But after the movie, we laughed about it a lot. It was a fun night. I still remember that day.

im2.text: One movie experience I'll never forget happened about three years ago. My friends and I went to see a big action movie on opening night. The theater was completely full, and everyone was really excited. But about thirty minutes into the movie, the screen suddenly went black. Nobody knew what was happening. We waited for about twenty minutes, and finally the staff told us there was a problem with the projector. They gave everyone free tickets for another day. We came back the next week and watched the whole movie. It was a little annoying, but now it's a funny story.

The most memorable movie experience I had was at an outdoor theater. Last fall, my coworkers and I went to a park where they showed a movie on a big screen at night. We brought blankets, snacks, and some drinks. The movie was an old romantic comedy, and I had already seen it before, but watching it under the stars felt completely different. It got really cold later, so we all shared our blankets. I think that night helped me become closer to my coworkers. I really want to go again this year.

im3.text: The movie experience I remember best was when I took my grandmother to the theater for the first time in many years. It was about two years ago. She hadn't been to a theater since she was young, because she always said it was too expensive. So for her eightieth birthday, I bought two tickets to a family drama. At first, she was surprised by how big the screen was and how loud the sound was. In the middle of the movie, I looked over and saw that she was crying. After the movie, she held my hand and told me it was the best gift she had received in a long time. I felt so proud and happy. Whenever I think about that day, it still warms my heart.
phrases: The movie experience I remember best

im3.text: One experience that stands out was when I fell asleep during a movie I had been waiting for all year. It was a science fiction movie, and I bought my ticket a month early. Unfortunately, the night before, I had to stay up late to finish a project at work, so I only slept about three hours. The movie started, and for the first hour I was fine, but then the room was dark and the seat was so comfortable. The next thing I knew, the credits were rolling and my friend was laughing at me. I was so disappointed, so I went back the next weekend and watched it again. Since then, I never go to a movie when I'm tired.

ih.text: The movie experience I remember most clearly happened during my first trip abroad, about four years ago. I was studying English in a small city overseas, and one rainy evening, a few classmates and I decided to go to a local theater. The movie was in English with no subtitles, and I was honestly nervous that I wouldn't understand anything. For the first twenty minutes or so, I was catching maybe half of the dialogue, but then something interesting happened. I stopped trying to translate every word and just followed the story through the acting and the music. By the end, I realized I had understood most of it, and I even laughed at a couple of jokes at the same time as the local audience. Walking back to the dormitory in the rain, I felt incredibly proud. It was the first moment I really believed my English was improving, and that feeling motivated me for the rest of my stay.

One movie night I'll never forget is the time I ended up watching a movie with complete strangers. It was a few years ago, during a big snowstorm. I had gone to a late show alone, and when the movie finished, we found out that the subway had stopped running and there were no taxis. The theater manager kindly let about fifteen of us stay in the lobby, and then he decided to play another movie for us, an old comedy, just to pass the time. At first, everyone was a little awkward, but halfway through, people started sharing snacks and laughing together. Afterward, we stayed up talking until the trains started again at five in the morning. I even exchanged numbers with two of them, and we still meet up sometimes. It's funny how a bad situation turned into one of my favorite memories.

al.text: The movie-watching experience that has stayed with me the longest happened when I was in high school, and it actually changed what I wanted to do with my life. Our class was taken on a field trip to see a documentary about doctors working in rural areas with almost no equipment. Most of my friends treated it as a chance to skip class, and honestly, so did I at first. But about twenty minutes in, there was a scene where a young doctor had to make a difficult decision with very little time, and I couldn't take my eyes off the screen. When the lights came on, the theater was unusually quiet. On the bus back to school, I kept thinking about how much one person could change in a small community. That night, I told my parents I wanted to study medicine, which surprised them, because I had never shown any interest before. I ended up majoring in nursing instead, but I genuinely believe that one afternoon in a dark theater set me on the path I'm on today.
phrases: has stayed with me the longest
I couldn't take my eyes off

al.text: I'd have to say the most memorable time was when my younger brother and I went to see a movie together right before he left for his military service. We hadn't been very close for a few years, mostly because we were both busy and, to be honest, we argued a lot. My mother suggested that we spend his last weekend doing something together, so I reluctantly bought tickets for a superhero movie he had been talking about. Before it started, we barely spoke, but during the movie, we kept glancing at each other and laughing at the same jokes, just like when we were kids. Afterward, instead of going straight home, we ended up sitting in a fast-food restaurant for three hours, talking about everything from our childhood to our plans for the future. It was the first real conversation we'd had in years. When he left a few days later, I felt surprisingly emotional. Looking back, the movie itself was pretty forgettable, but that evening completely changed our relationship.

questions.tip_ko: 언제, 누구와, 무슨 일이 있었는지를 과거형으로 차례대로 말해요. 마지막에 그때 느낀 점이나 지금 생각을 한 문장 붙여요.

questions.question: How has the way people watch movies changed compared to when you were younger? Compare how you watched movies in the past with how you watch them now, and explain what caused these changes.

il.text: In the past, I watched movies at the theater. Now I watch movies on my phone. It is easy. It is cheap. But the screen is small. I like the theater more, but I go less.
When I was young, I watched movies on TV with my family. Now I watch movies alone on my laptop. I choose the movie. It is convenient. But I miss my family time.

im1.text: When I was a child, I watched movies at the theater with my family about once a month. It was a special event. Now, I usually watch movies at home on my laptop, because I can watch any movie anytime. It is cheaper and more comfortable. But I think going to the theater was more exciting. I want to go to the theater more often.

In the past, people rented DVDs from a store to watch movies at home. I remember going to a rental shop with my father every Friday. Now, we don't need to go anywhere. We just choose a movie online and watch it on TV. It is much easier. But I miss the rental shop, because choosing a movie together was fun.

im2.text: The way I watch movies has changed a lot. When I was in middle school, I went to the theater with my friends almost every weekend, and a movie ticket was quite cheap. These days, tickets are expensive, so I usually watch movies at home on online services. I can pause the movie, eat whatever I want, and watch in my pajamas. I think the biggest reason for this change is the internet. Fast internet made it easy to watch new movies at home. However, I still go to the theater for big action movies, because the experience is different.
phrases: the biggest reason for this change

im2.text: When I was younger, I watched movies on a big TV in the living room with my whole family. We all had to agree on one movie, so we usually watched family movies. Now, everyone in my family has a smartphone, so we watch different movies on our own screens, even in the same room. It's more convenient, because I can watch what I want. In the past, we always talked about the movie after it ended. But I feel a little sad, because we don't talk about movies together anymore. I think smartphones changed how families spend their time.

im3.text: Compared to when I was a teenager, the way I watch movies is completely different. Back then, going to the theater was the only way to see a new movie, so it felt like a big event. My friends and I would plan it days in advance and spend the whole afternoon downtown. Nowadays, I mostly watch movies at home through online streaming. New movies come out online just a few weeks after they're in theaters, so I don't feel the need to rush. I think the main reasons are convenience and price. A monthly subscription costs about the same as one movie ticket. The downside is that I get distracted more easily at home, and I sometimes check my phone in the middle of a movie, which never happened at the theater.

When I was a kid, watching a movie meant sitting down for two hours and finishing the whole thing. Now, I notice that I watch movies in small pieces. For example, I might watch thirty minutes on the subway in the morning and finish the rest before bed. I think this change happened because of smartphones and busy schedules. People don't have long blocks of free time anymore, so they fit movies into short breaks. Another big change is that I watch a lot of movies with subtitles from other countries now, which was rare when I was young. Overall, I have more choices than ever, but I feel like I enjoy each movie a little less deeply than before.
phrases: I think this change happened because

ih.text: Looking back, the way I watch movies has changed in almost every way. When I was in elementary school, watching a movie was a family event. My father would rent a video on Friday night, and all four of us would squeeze onto the sofa together. Then, in high school, going to the theater with friends became the main way to see movies, and it was the center of our weekend plans. These days, though, most of my movie watching happens alone, on a tablet, often late at night in bed. I think there are two main reasons for this. First, streaming services have made almost any movie available instantly, so there's no reason to wait or go out. Second, my schedule is much busier, and it's hard to find a time that works for everyone. Honestly, I enjoy the freedom, but I sometimes miss the feeling of laughing together in a crowded room. That's why I still try to go to the theater with friends at least once a month.
phrases: there are two main reasons for this

ih.text: I'd say the biggest difference between then and now is how I choose movies. When I was younger, I didn't have many options. There were only a few movies playing at the local theater, and we just picked whichever one had the best poster. Sometimes we ended up watching something terrible, but it was part of the fun. Now, I have thousands of movies available on several streaming apps, and I spend a ridiculous amount of time just scrolling through the list. Some nights, I scroll for thirty minutes and then give up and go to sleep. I also rely heavily on ratings and recommendations now, which means I rarely take a chance on something unusual. I think technology is the main cause, since apps suggest movies based on what I've already watched. It's convenient, but I feel like my taste has become narrower. Recently, I've started asking friends for recommendations instead, just to break out of that pattern.

al.text: The change has been huge, and in some ways I think it reflects how society as a whole has changed. When I was growing up, movies were something you experienced with other people. Going to the theater meant dressing up a little, buying tickets at the counter, and sitting in a room full of strangers who laughed and gasped at the same moments. Even at home, the whole family gathered around one television. Today, the experience is much more personal and, honestly, a bit isolated. I usually watch movies alone on my tablet, and I can pause, skip, or quit whenever I feel like it. The main driver, obviously, is streaming technology, but I think lifestyle changes matter just as much. People work longer hours and have less predictable schedules, so watching on demand simply fits better. There are clear advantages, like being able to watch films from all over the world that would never have reached a local theater. Still, I can't help feeling that we've lost something. A movie you watch in a packed theater becomes a shared memory, while one you watch alone on a small screen tends to fade a lot faster.

If I compare my childhood with today, the biggest difference isn't really where I watch movies but how much attention I give them. As a kid, a movie was a rare treat. My parents allowed us to watch one movie on Saturday night, so I gave it my complete focus, and I'd often watch the same few movies again and again until I knew the lines by heart. Nowadays, movies are everywhere and basically unlimited, so they've become a kind of background activity. I'll have something playing while I cook or answer messages, and sometimes I realize I've missed half the plot. I think this happened partly because of streaming and partly because smartphones have trained us to switch between things constantly. To be fair, the variety today is incredible, and I've discovered amazing films from countries I knew nothing about. But I've recently started a small rule for myself. Once a week, I watch one movie with my phone in another room, the way I did as a child. It's surprising how much more I enjoy it, and how much longer I remember it afterward.
phrases: partly because of ~ and partly because

questions.tip_ko: 예전에는 어땠는지, 지금은 어떤지, 왜 바뀌었는지 세 부분으로 나눠 말해요. In the past, Nowadays 같은 표현으로 시점을 분명히 해요.

questions.question: You indicated in the survey that you like listening to music. What kind of music do you enjoy? Tell me about your favorite type of music and the singers or musicians you like, and explain why.

il.text: I like pop music. Pop songs are easy and fun. I listen to pop music every day. I like female singers. Their voices are beautiful. When I listen to pop music, I feel good.
My favorite music is ballad. Ballads are slow and quiet. I listen to them at night. The songs are about love. I like a Korean singer with a soft voice. Ballads help me relax.

im1.text: I like many kinds of music, but my favorite is pop music. Pop songs have catchy melodies, so I can sing along easily. I usually listen to pop music on my phone when I go to work. My favorite singer is a female pop singer with a strong voice. Her songs always give me energy in the morning. I also like dance music, because it makes me want to move.

My favorite type of music is jazz. I started listening to jazz in university. Jazz is relaxing, and it is good when I study or read. I like the sound of the piano and the saxophone. I usually listen to jazz at a café or at home in the evening. It makes me calm. I don't know many jazz musicians, but I enjoy the music.
phrases: My favorite type of music is

im2.text: I enjoy listening to many kinds of music, but my favorite is hip-hop. I like hip-hop because the lyrics are very honest. Many rappers talk about their real lives, their problems, and their dreams. When I listen carefully, I feel like they are telling me a story. I also like the strong beat, because it gives me energy when I work out at the gym. My favorite rapper is a young Korean artist who writes all of his own songs. I think his lyrics are really smart. So hip-hop is the music I listen to the most.

I usually listen to classical music. Many people think classical music is boring, but I think it's very peaceful. I started listening to it in high school when I was studying for exams, because songs with lyrics made it hard to concentrate. Now I listen to classical music almost every day, especially piano music. My favorite composer is from the eighteenth century, and his music is bright and happy. When I feel stressed, I put on my headphones, close my eyes, and listen for a while. Then I feel much better.

im3.text: I listen to all kinds of music, but if I had to choose one, it would be indie rock. I like indie music because it feels more personal than the songs on the top charts. The bands are usually small, and they write their own songs about everyday life, like missing a friend or feeling tired after work. I found my favorite band by chance about three years ago, when a friend played one of their songs in the car. I immediately asked her for the name of the band. Since then, I've listened to all of their albums, and I even went to one of their small concerts last year. Their music always makes me feel like I'm not alone, which is why I love it so much.
phrases: if I had to choose one
I found my favorite band by chance

im3.text: My favorite kind of music is movie soundtracks, which might sound a little unusual. I love them because they bring back the feeling of the movie. For example, when I hear the main theme from an adventure movie I watched as a kid, I immediately feel excited, like I'm about to go on a journey. I also find soundtracks really useful when I study or work, because most of them don't have lyrics, but they still have a lot of emotion. My favorite composer writes music for big fantasy movies, and his songs are dramatic, with lots of strings and drums. I usually listen to soundtracks on long bus rides. It makes the trip feel like a scene from a movie.
phrases: which might sound a little unusual

ih.text: I'd describe myself as a pretty big fan of R&B. I first got into it in high school, when my older brother kept playing R&B songs in the room we shared. At first, I thought it was too slow, but after a while, I started to notice how smooth and emotional the singing was. What I love most about R&B is the voice. Good R&B singers can change the mood of a whole song with just a small change in their tone. I also like that the songs are often about relationships, so it's easy to connect them to my own life. My favorite singer is a male vocalist with a really warm, deep voice, and I've probably listened to his latest album a hundred times. These days, I mostly listen to R&B at night when I'm winding down after work. It helps me slow down and clear my head before going to bed.

Honestly, my music taste is a bit old-fashioned. My favorite type of music is classic rock from the seventies and eighties. I got into it because of my father, who used to play his old records every Sunday morning while he cleaned the house. Back then, I didn't really pay attention, but when I was in university, I found one of his old albums and listened to it properly for the first time. I was surprised by how powerful the guitar sounded and how meaningful the lyrics were. Compared to a lot of music today, classic rock feels more raw and real, because the bands played their instruments live without much editing. Now I have my own collection of records, and whenever I visit my parents, my father and I listen to music together. It's become a special way for us to connect.
phrases: my music taste is a bit old-fashioned
I got into it because of

al.text: My taste in music is pretty wide, but the genre I keep coming back to is acoustic folk music, the kind with just a guitar, maybe a violin, and a singer telling a story. I think what draws me to it is the simplicity. There's nothing to hide behind, no heavy effects or complicated production, so the quality of the songwriting and the voice really comes through. A lot of folk songs are basically short stories about ordinary people, like a farmer who loses his land or two old friends meeting again after many years, and I find those stories surprisingly moving. My favorite musician is a singer-songwriter who performs mostly in small venues. I discovered her at a street festival a few years ago, and I was so impressed that I bought her album right there. I usually listen to folk music on quiet weekend mornings with a cup of coffee, and it sets a calm tone for the whole day. In a world that feels noisy and fast most of the time, this kind of music reminds me to slow down.
phrases: the genre I keep coming back to

al.text: I'd say my favorite type of music is electronic music, although that's a pretty broad category, so let me explain what I mean. I'm not really into the loud club music that most people imagine. What I enjoy is the more atmospheric kind, with layered synthesizers and steady beats that slowly build up over several minutes. I started listening to it while I was preparing for a big exam, because I needed something without lyrics that could keep me focused for hours, and it worked better than anything else I tried. Over time, I became genuinely interested in how the music is made, so I even downloaded a free music program and tried creating a few simple tracks myself. They were pretty terrible, but it gave me a lot more respect for the artists. These days, I listen to electronic music almost every day, mostly when I'm working or running. It has this way of blocking out distractions and putting me in a kind of flow state, which is exactly what I need on busy days.
phrases: let me explain what I mean
which is exactly what I need

questions.tip_ko: 장르 하나와 좋아하는 가수의 특징(목소리, 가사)을 말해요. 언제 처음 좋아하게 됐는지 짧은 이야기를 붙이면 좋아요.

questions.question: When and where do you usually listen to music? Tell me about your typical day and how music fits into it. What devices do you use, and how do you find new songs?

il.text: I listen to music every morning. I use my phone and earphones. I listen on the bus. I also listen at night. I find new songs on music apps. I like this routine.
I listen to music at home. I use a small speaker. I listen when I cook and clean. Music makes cleaning fun. My friends tell me new songs. I listen to them on the weekend.
phrases: I listen to music at home

im1.text: I listen to music almost all day. In the morning, I listen to music on my phone while I go to work by subway. At work, I can't listen to music, but at lunchtime I sometimes listen to a few songs. In the evening, I play music on a speaker while I cook dinner. I usually find new songs from the music app's recommendations. It's very easy.

I usually listen to music when I exercise. I go to the gym three times a week, and I always wear my wireless earphones. I listen to fast songs, because they help me run longer. I also listen to music before I go to sleep, but I choose slow songs at night. To find new songs, I check the music chart every Monday.
phrases: I usually listen to music when

im2.text: Music is a big part of my daily routine. When I wake up, I turn on the radio while I get ready for work. I like the morning radio show because the host plays different songs every day. On my way to work, I listen to my own playlist with my earphones. At the office, I sometimes listen to quiet music without lyrics when I need to focus. After work, I usually relax with music on my sofa. I find most of my new songs through the radio or from my friends, who send me links in our group chat.
phrases: is a big part of my daily routine
I find most of my new songs

im2.text: I listen to music mostly when I'm moving from one place to another. I take the bus for about forty minutes to get to school, so music helps the time pass quickly. I use my smartphone and a pair of headphones that block outside noise. I usually make a different playlist for each season. For example, in winter I listen to more calm and warm songs. On weekends, I like to listen to music at a café while I study. To find new songs, I watch music videos online, and when I like a song, I add it to my playlist right away.

im3.text: My day pretty much has a soundtrack. The first thing I do after I wake up is play an upbeat playlist on my bedroom speaker, because it helps me get out of bed. While I commute, I usually switch to podcasts or calm music, depending on my mood. During the workday, I can't really listen to music since I'm in meetings a lot, but I listen during my lunch walk. The evening is my favorite time for music. I put on a record, make a simple dinner, and just enjoy it. As for finding new music, I mostly rely on the recommendation lists in my music app, but honestly, my best discoveries usually come from my coworker, who has amazing taste. She sends me a new song almost every week.
phrases: My day pretty much has a soundtrack

im3.text: I don't listen to music all day like some people, but I have a few special times for it. The first is in the morning when I'm running in the park. I always use my sports earphones and play a high-energy playlist, which keeps me going. The second is when I'm doing housework on the weekend. I connect my phone to a speaker and play music loudly, and somehow cleaning doesn't feel so boring anymore. The last one is late at night, when I listen to soft songs before sleeping. When it comes to new songs, I often discover them in coffee shops. If I hear something I like, I use an app on my phone to find out the title. I've found many of my favorite songs that way.
phrases: I have a few special times for it

ih.text: Music is pretty much always playing in my life, but the type changes depending on the time of day. In the morning, I listen to something light and positive while I make breakfast, usually through a small speaker in my kitchen. My commute is about an hour by subway, so that's when I do most of my serious listening. I put on noise-canceling headphones and listen to full albums from start to finish, because I think that's how artists want their music to be heard. At work, I keep instrumental music on low volume when I'm writing reports. In the evening, I often have music playing in the background while I cook or chat with my roommate. To find new music, I follow a few music critics online and check their weekly recommendations. I also go to small live shows about once a month, and I've discovered some great local bands there.
phrases: depending on the time of day
that's when I do most of

ih.text: To be honest, I've become a bit more intentional about music recently. I used to have music playing all day without really listening to it, but I realized it was just background noise. So now I set aside specific times. On weekday mornings, I listen to one new album during my commute, and I actually pay attention to the lyrics and the arrangement. At night, I spend about twenty minutes listening to vinyl records on an old record player I bought from a secondhand shop. It forces me to sit still and focus, since I have to flip the record halfway through. On weekends, I sometimes go to a record store just to browse. The staff there are really knowledgeable, and they often recommend albums I'd never find online. This new routine has made listening to music feel like a real hobby again, not just something that fills the silence.
phrases: I've become a bit more intentional about

al.text: Music runs through basically my entire day, though the role it plays changes a lot from morning to night. As soon as I wake up, I ask the smart speaker in my bedroom to play a morning playlist, mostly upbeat pop, which honestly does more to wake me up than coffee does. During my commute, I switch to headphones and use that time for new releases, because it's the one part of the day when I can give music my full attention. Once I get to the office, things change. I need to concentrate, so I stick to instrumental tracks at a very low volume, things like lo-fi beats or quiet piano. In the evening, music becomes more social. My roommate and I take turns choosing songs while we cook, and it often turns into a friendly argument about whose taste is better. As for discovering new music, I've learned not to rely only on app algorithms, since they tend to recommend the same style over and over. Instead, I listen to a weekly radio show hosted by a music journalist, and I make a point of trying at least one genre I don't normally listen to every month.
phrases: runs through basically my entire day
Once I get to the office

al.text: My relationship with music is pretty structured, partly because I play the piano myself, so listening is connected to practicing. I usually start the day by listening to a piece I'm learning, ideally a few different recordings of it, so I can compare how various pianists interpret the same notes. I do that on the train with good headphones, and I often take short notes on my phone about the tempo or the mood. During the day, I mostly avoid music, because I find it distracting at work. Then, after dinner, I practice for about an hour, and once I'm done, I reward myself by listening to something completely different, like jazz or soul, just for pleasure. When it comes to finding new music, I rely a lot on live performances. I try to attend at least one concert a month, often small ones at local music schools, which are surprisingly good and usually cheap. I've also joined an online community where people share recordings and discuss them, and that's become my main source of recommendations. For me, music isn't just entertainment. It's something I study, enjoy, and share at the same time.

questions.tip_ko: 아침, 이동할 때, 저녁처럼 시간 순서로 말하고, 어떤 기기를 쓰는지와 새 노래를 찾는 방법까지 빠뜨리지 말고 답해요.

questions.question: Tell me about a memorable experience you had related to music. It could be a concert you went to or a special moment with a song. What happened, and why do you still remember it?

il.text: Last year, I went to a concert. It was in a big stadium. There were many people. The singer was very good. I sang along. I was so happy. I want to go again.
I remember my school music festival. I was fifteen. I played the guitar with my friends. I was nervous. But we did a good job. Everyone clapped. I was proud.

im1.text: Two years ago, I went to my first concert with my best friend. It was an outdoor concert in summer. We waited in line for three hours, and it was very hot. But when the singer came on stage, everyone screamed. I sang along to every song. After the concert, my voice was gone, but I was really happy. It was an amazing night.

I remember a special song from my high school graduation. My class sang a song together at the ceremony. We practiced for one month. On the day, many students cried while we were singing, because we were sad to say goodbye. Now, when I hear that song, I remember my friends and teachers. It is still my favorite song, and I sing it sometimes.

im2.text: The most memorable music experience I had was at a jazz festival last fall. My friend had an extra ticket, so she invited me, even though I didn't know much about jazz. The festival was on an island, and we had to take a ferry to get there. We sat on the grass and listened to many bands all day. In the evening, a band played a slow song while the sun was going down, and everyone became quiet. It was so beautiful. After that day, I started listening to jazz, and now it's one of my favorite types of music.

I remember when I sang at my older sister's wedding. It was about three years ago. My sister asked me to sing a song for her, and I said yes, but I was really nervous because I'm not a good singer. I practiced every night for a month. On the wedding day, my hands were shaking, and I forgot some of the words in the middle of the song. But everyone clapped loudly, and my sister cried. Later, she told me it was the best part of the wedding. I'll never forget that moment.

im3.text: One music experience I'll never forget was a concert I went to by myself in another city. It was about two years ago. My favorite band only had one show in my country, and none of my friends liked them, so I decided to go alone. I took an early train and arrived four hours before the show. While I was waiting in line, I started talking with the people around me, and we found out we liked the same songs. By the time the concert started, we were like old friends, and we sang together all night. After the concert, we went out for late-night noodles. I was worried about going alone, but it turned out to be one of the best days of my life.

A memorable music moment for me happened in a very ordinary place, a small coffee shop near my old apartment. It was a rainy evening, and I was feeling really down because I had just failed an important job interview. While I was sitting there, the café played an old song that my grandmother used to sing to me when I was little. I hadn't heard it in more than ten years. Suddenly, I remembered her warm voice and how she always told me not to give up. I actually started crying a little in the café. After the song ended, I felt much calmer. A month later, I got a different job, and I still think of that song as a lucky charm.
phrases: happened in a very ordinary place

ih.text: The music experience that stands out most for me happened when I was volunteering at a nursing home during university. Every Saturday, a few students and I visited to spend time with the elderly residents, and one week, someone suggested we play some old songs for them. I could play the guitar a little, so I learned a few classic songs from the sixties. Honestly, I didn't expect much of a reaction. But when I started playing, an old man who almost never spoke began singing along, and he knew every single word. The staff told me he hadn't been that lively in months. After that, I brought my guitar every week, and it became a small concert that everyone looked forward to. That experience taught me that music can reach people in a way that words sometimes can't. It's still one of the most meaningful things I've ever done.

I'd have to say my most memorable experience with music was my very first time performing on stage. It was at a small open-mic night in a bar near my university about four years ago. I had been teaching myself the keyboard for a year, and my friends kept pushing me to perform in front of people. I finally agreed and chose a slow song I had written myself. When my name was called, my heart was beating so fast that I could barely hear the music. Halfway through, I made a big mistake and played a completely wrong chord. I almost stopped, but I took a breath and kept going. When I finished, the audience clapped and a stranger came up to say the song had touched her. That night gave me so much confidence, and I've performed about ten more times since then.

al.text: The one that immediately comes to mind is a concert I went to with my father a few years ago, which ended up being much more meaningful than either of us expected. He had loved a particular rock band since he was a teenager, but he had never seen them live, because back then he couldn't afford tickets, and later he was too busy raising a family. When I found out the band was doing a reunion tour, I secretly bought two tickets for his sixtieth birthday. I still remember the look on his face when I gave him the envelope. He tried to act calm, but his hands were shaking. At the concert, the man I'd always known as quiet and serious was jumping, shouting, and singing every lyric. Near the end, the band played the song he used to sing in the car when I was little, and he turned to me with tears in his eyes. On the drive home, he told me stories about his youth that I had never heard before. That night didn't just give him a concert. It gave me a completely new side of my father.
phrases: The one that immediately comes to mind

al.text: One experience that genuinely changed how I think about music happened during a trip abroad about three years ago. I was walking through an old town late in the evening when I heard a group of street musicians playing traditional folk music in a small square. There were maybe five of them, with violins, an accordion, and a drum, and a crowd had gathered around. What struck me was that people of all ages were dancing together, from little kids to elderly couples, even though most of them clearly didn't know each other. I didn't understand a single word of the songs, but the energy was impossible to resist, and before I knew it, an old woman grabbed my hands and pulled me into the circle. I ended up dancing for almost an hour. Looking back, I think it showed me that music doesn't need a shared language to bring people together. Since that night, I've made a habit of looking for local live music wherever I travel, and it's become my favorite way to get to know a place.
phrases: genuinely changed how I think about

questions.tip_ko: 장소와 상황을 먼저 설명하고, 일어난 일을 시간 순서대로 과거형으로 말해요. 그 경험이 나에게 남긴 것으로 마무리해요.

questions.question: Think about the music you listened to when you were a teenager and the music you listen to now. How has your taste in music changed? Compare the two and explain what led to the change.

il.text: When I was a teenager, I listened to dance music. It was fast. Now I listen to slow music. It is relaxing. I am older now. I like quiet songs more.
In the past, I liked idol groups. I bought their albums. Now I like ballads. I listen to music on my phone. I don't buy albums now. My taste changed.

im1.text: When I was a teenager, I listened to idol music all the time. I liked dancing to their songs with my friends. Now, I listen to more calm music like acoustic songs and ballads. I think I changed because my life is busier now, and I need music to relax. Also, I listen to music on my phone now, not on an MP3 player.

In my teens, I only listened to Korean pop music. I didn't listen to foreign songs because I couldn't understand the lyrics. Now, I listen to many English songs, because my English is better. I also like songs from other countries. My taste is much wider than before. I think studying English changed my music taste. Music also helps me study English.

im2.text: My taste in music has changed a lot since I was a teenager. Back then, I loved loud rock music. I listened to it really loudly in my room, and my mom always told me to turn it down. These days, I prefer jazz and soft pop. I think the main reason is my job. I work in a busy office, and after work I just want something calm. Another reason is that my friends changed. In high school, my friends liked rock, but now my coworkers like jazz, so I learned about it from them.
phrases: I think the main reason is

im2.text: When I was a teenager, I listened to whatever was popular on the music charts. I just wanted to know the same songs as my friends. Now, I care more about my own taste. I listen to small indie bands that most people don't know. I think this changed because of music apps. The apps recommend songs based on what I like, so I discover new artists every week. Also, I care less about what other people think now. I'm happy that I found my own style, and I enjoy music more than before.
phrases: I think this changed because of

im3.text: Comparing my teenage years to now, my music taste has become much more relaxed. When I was in high school, I was really into heavy metal. I loved the fast guitar and the screaming vocals, and I think it helped me let out my stress from studying. I even dyed my hair red once to look like a metal singer. Now, in my thirties, I mostly listen to acoustic music and jazz. I think the biggest reason is that my lifestyle changed. I don't have exam stress anymore, but I'm tired after work, so I need music that calms me down. Also, I live in an apartment with thin walls, so playing loud music isn't really an option. Sometimes I still listen to metal, though, especially when I need energy at the gym.
phrases: I think the biggest reason is

im3.text: My taste in music has actually become more open over the years. As a teenager, I was pretty narrow-minded about music. I only listened to hip-hop, and I used to think other genres were boring. Now, I listen to almost everything, including classical, country, and even old trot songs that my parents like. I think a few things caused this change. First, I lived abroad for a year, and I met people from many countries who introduced me to their music. Second, streaming services made it easy to try new genres for free. Finally, I think I just became more curious as I got older. Looking back, I feel like I missed a lot of great music when I was young.
phrases: I think a few things caused this change

ih.text: There's a big difference between the music I listened to as a teenager and what I listen to now, and I think it mirrors how I've changed as a person. In middle and high school, I was obsessed with boy bands. I knew every member's name and birthday, and I spent most of my allowance on albums and posters. For me, music was really about belonging, because being a fan connected me with my friends. These days, I'm much more drawn to singer-songwriters, especially those who write about real-life struggles like work, loneliness, or getting older. I care much more about lyrics now than about how a singer looks. I'd say the main reason is simply growing up. Once I started working and living on my own, those songs about everyday life started to feel much more relatable. That said, I still have a soft spot for my old favorite band, and when one of their songs comes on, I instantly feel sixteen again.
phrases: I'd say the main reason is

ih.text: My music taste has changed in a direction I never would have expected. When I was a teenager, I couldn't stand classical music. My parents made me take piano lessons, and I hated practicing, so I associated classical music with boredom and pressure. I listened mostly to electronic dance music instead, because it felt modern and exciting. But about five years ago, I watched a documentary about a famous orchestra, and something clicked. I started listening to the pieces I used to play on the piano, and I realized how beautiful they actually were. Now, classical music is probably half of what I listen to.
